skill.title: Prove triangles congruent (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS)

steps.title: Pick out the matching parts of the two triangles

lines.text: $|OA| = |OB|$, because $p$ makes equal intercepts on the axes.
$|OC| = |OC|$, because it is a common side.
$|\angle OCA| = |\angle BCO| = 90^\circ$, because $q \perp p$ and $C$ lies on both lines.

steps.title: State the congruence

lines.text: Each triangle has a right angle, a hypotenuse ($[OA]$ and $[OB]$ are equal) and one other equal side ($[OC]$).
This is the RHS (right angle, hypotenuse, side) condition, so the triangles $OCA$ and $OBC$ are congruent.

steps.title: Statement A: similar triangles must be congruent

lines.text: Tick false.
Similar triangles have the same shape (equal angles) but can be different sizes.
A small triangle and a large triangle can have the same angles, so they are not identical.

steps.title: Statement B: congruent triangles must be similar

lines.text: Tick true.
Congruent triangles have all sides and angles equal, so every feature is identical.
Their angles are therefore the same, which makes them similar.

steps.title: Use the angle in a semicircle

lines.text: $[AB]$ is a diameter, so the angle at $D$ on the circle is a right angle.

steps.title: Use the angle in a semicircle

lines.text: $[AB]$ is a diameter, so the angle at $D$ in the semicircle is a right angle.

steps.title: Use the isosceles triangle ABD

lines.text: Triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with the right angle at $D$, so $|AD| = |DB|$ and the two base angles are equal.

steps.title: Use angles standing on the same arc

lines.text: $\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$ both stand on the arc $AD$, so they are equal.

steps.title: Angles in triangle ADC add to 180 degrees
(i) Explain why the angle CBD is 90 degrees

lines.text: The diagram is symmetrical about $DC$, so $[CD]$ passes through the centre of the circle and is a diameter.
$B$ is on the circle, so $\angle CBD$ is an angle at the circumference standing on the diameter $[CD]$.
The angle in a semicircle is $90^\circ$, so $|\angle CBD| = 90^\circ$.

steps.title: (ii) Find the first pair of equal angles

lines.text: By symmetry about $DC$, $[CD]$ is perpendicular to $[AB]$ at $E$.
So $|\angle CEB| = |\angle DEB|$ (both are $90^\circ$).

steps.title: Find the second pair of equal angles

lines.text: In triangle $BCD$, $|\angle CBD| = 90^\circ$, so $|\angle BCD|$ and $|\angle BDC|$ add to $90^\circ$.
In triangle $BED$, $|\angle DEB| = 90^\circ$, so $|\angle DBE|$ and $|\angle EDB|$ add to $90^\circ$.
So $|\angle ECB| = |\angle DBE|$.

steps.title: Find the third pair and conclude

lines.text: Angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$, so the remaining angles are equal: $|\angle CBE| = |\angle BDE|$.
Triangles $BCE$ and $DBE$ have all three angles equal, so they are similar.

steps.title: Find a right angle in each triangle

lines.text: $[BD] \perp [AC]$, so both triangles have a right angle at $B$.

steps.title: Use the angle in a semicircle

lines.text: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so $\angle ADC$ is $90^\circ$.

steps.title: Use the angle sum in triangle DBC

lines.text: Angles in triangle $DBC$ add to $180^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = 90^\circ$.

steps.title: Compare the two equations

lines.text: Both sums equal $90^\circ$ and both contain $|\angle BDC|$.
Subtract $|\angle BDC|$ from both sides.

steps.title: State the conclusion

lines.text: Two angles of $ABD$ equal two angles of $DBC$ ($90^\circ$ at $B$, and $\angle ADB = \angle BCD$), so the triangles are equiangular, hence similar.
